rounds.hypothesis: Both pots should settle on the stove at origin z about 0.9965 m while remaining in the accepted region. Splitting them along site x by 0.11 m preserves roughly 0.0286 m nominal collision clearance. Moka pot 2 is placed first on the right, then moka pot 1 on the left with elevated transport to clear the first pot. The stove turn-on predicate already holds initially, so no unsupported fixture action is required.

All four development failures occurred before motion at moka_pot_2's approach: each registered-reference run supplied only one candidate, and that candidate was rejected during descent for collision with moka_pot_2 itself, with approximately 0.0021-0.0022 m penetration at grasp. The placement geometry, order, and heights were never exercised, so they are unchanged. I removed both single-candidate grasp_reference_id overrides, allowing the executor's normal collision-checked grasp planner to select feasible top-down grasps. Moka pot 2 remains first on the right and moka pot 1 second on the left. The stove turn-on predicate already holds and requires no unsupported action.

Placement, height, yaw, order, and predicates were correct: three development inits completed with all goals true, and the stove was already on. The sole failure was moka_pot_2's grasp guard in init 2: its only feasible default candidate, yaw 0/lateral 0.03/dz 0.04, was rejected after close for right-gripper contact with the target, after which no candidate remained. I therefore changed only grasp search, replacing the unrestricted default grid with a focused grid that retains the successful 0.04 m candidates and adds 0.05 and 0.06 m grasp heights on both observed lateral sides. The added vertical clearance should prevent candidate exhaustion while preserving the validated placement geometry.
